rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=3.5, img_sy=3.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-14: ONE knob changed vs the iter-13 WIN base (image-domain SPATIAL bilateral sigma img_sx/img_sy 2.5->3.5, BOTH x and y together = the isotropic image-domain spatial-extent sigma); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_13.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct, proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx/sy=1.0/2.0, proj_sr=0.02, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 -> identical seed=42 val split, directly comparable to iter-13). PUSH THE SAME WINNING LEVER FURTHER. Read iter-13 BY SSIM/HEADROOM (campaign primary; SSIM is the surface the spatial lever moved): iter-13 widened img_sx/img_sy 1.5->2.5 and LIFTED SSIM 0.7796->0.7940 (+0.0144, the run best), while hr stayed FLAT at 0.3332 (~iter-6 0.3330) -- the image-domain SPATIAL sigma is the FIRST lever in the whole run to break the SSIM plateau (img_n_bf depth had saturated SSIM growth and hr; proj domain fully inert at iter-11/12). FAILURE MODE iter-13 addressed and this iter re-probes: the 7-deep image bilateral cascade was UNDER-SMOOTHING the broad post-FBP noise floor at the default spatial sigma 1.5 -- widening the spatial neighborhood (sigma 1.5->2.5) let each of the 7 image BFs average over a larger support and smooth that broad noise floor, lifting the structural-similarity term while the LOOSE img_sr=0.02 kept it edge-preserving (no blur across phantom edges). The open question: does the image-domain spatial sigma KEEP lifting SSIM past 0.7940 as it widens further (3.5), or does it SATURATE / regress? HYPOTHESIS (img-spatial-2): widening img_sx/img_sy 2.5->3.5 enlarges the averaging support further, smoothing the residual noise floor more -> may lift SSIM above iter-13 0.7940 on the SAME seed=42 split (note whether hr moves too -- iter-13 SSIM rose but hr stayed 0.333, so the spatial lever may be an SSIM-only axis bounded by the same 64-view-FBP hr ceiling). KEY DIAGNOSTIC / RISK: img_kernel is held at 5, so the discrete bilateral WINDOW is +/-2 px. At sigma 2.5 the Gaussian spatial weight is already near-flat across that 5-px window (iter-13 noted 2.5 is near the window edge); at sigma 3.5 the spatial weight is even FLATTER -> the kernel=5 window, not the sigma, may now be the binding constraint, in which case SSIM saturates (or moves only marginally) because the BF can't actually reach the wider support the sigma requests. If SSIM SATURATES or regresses here, that pinpoints img_kernel (window SIZE) as the iter-15 lever -- widen img_kernel 5->7/9 to let the larger spatial sigma act over a genuinely larger window (the pre-registered next step from iter-13's rationale: 'img_kernel is the iter-14 candidate if img_sx/sy moves hr' -- img_sx/sy DID move SSIM, so kernel is now the live follow-on once sigma saturates). If SSIM KEEPS rising, the spatial sigma still has headroom inside the kernel=5 window and iter-15 pushes sigma further (4.5) before touching the kernel. Chose img_sx/img_sy 2.5->3.5 (the SAME winning lever, one notch further -- the steer's explicit instruction) over (a) img_kernel (the natural follow-on, but only AFTER confirming whether sigma alone saturates inside the current window -- changing kernel now would confound the sigma-saturation question), (b) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (c) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction -- tightening collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, do NOT tighten; stays LOOSE 0.02), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (e) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-13 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-13 ran well under budget; img_sx/img_sy are pure init sigma values inside the fixed img_kernel=5 window -> ZERO added compute, wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.
